s2693: In Georgia, drivers' working and rest times are regulated in accordance with the requirements of the European Agreement concerning the Work of Crews of Vehicles Engaged in International Road Transport (AETR).

s2801: According to subparagraphs "a", "d" and "e" of paragraph 3 of Article 30 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, road traffic is controlled by authorised officials of the Ministry of Internal Affairs of Georgia. Within the powers granted to them by the legislation of Georgia, road traffic may also be controlled by: a) authorised officials of the Ministry of Defence of Georgia, when convoys of vehicles belonging to the Ministry of Defence of Georgia are moving; d) members of an ambulance team, when providing emergency medical care; e) the escort (accompanying adult) of a group of children, to ensure the children's safety.
s2802: When the escort of a group of children signals to do so, must the driver give way to the children crossing the carriageway?
s2803: According to paragraph 5 of Article 26 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, when the escort of a group of children signals to do so, the driver must give way to the children crossing the carriageway.

s2807: On unlit roads in built-up areas and on roads outside built-up areas, groups of children may be led along the road:
s2808: According to paragraph 5 of Article 26 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, groups of children may be led along unlit roads in built-up areas and along roads outside built-up areas only in daylight.
s2812: When a group of children is being led along the road, the group must be divided into rows of no more than:
s2813: According to paragraph 5 of Article 26 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, groups of children must be led by an adult escort, and the group must be divided into rows of no more than two children.
s2816: When carrying a child under 3 on the rear seat of a passenger car, is it mandatory to use a special child carrycot, seat or restraint, except when the child is sitting on the lap of a passenger aged at least 16 who is sitting on the rear seat and holding only that child?
s2817: According to paragraphs 7 and 8 of Article 26 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic: 7. Except in the cases specified in paragraph 8 of this Article, when a child under 3 is carried on the rear seat of a passenger car, a special child carrycot, seat or restraint suited to the child's height and weight must be used. 8. A child under 3 may be carried on the lap of a passenger aged at least 16 sitting on the rear seat of a passenger car, provided that this passenger is holding only that child.
s2818: Is it prohibited to carry passengers (not counting children under 12) if their number exceeds the number allowed by the vehicle's technical specifications?
s2819: According to subparagraph "b" of paragraph 10 of Article 46 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, carrying passengers is prohibited if their number exceeds the number allowed by the vehicle's technical specifications (not counting children under 12).
s2824: Riding a bicycle or a two-wheeled electric scooter on the road is permitted:
s2825: According to paragraph 1 of Article 43 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, riding a bicycle or a two-wheeled electric scooter on the road is permitted for persons aged at least 14, and riding a moped for persons aged 16.
s2826: Which of these road signs warns of a section of road near a children's facility, where children are likely to appear on the carriageway?
s2827: According to paragraph 1.24 of Chapter 1 (Warning signs) of Annex 1 to the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, road sign 1.24 "Children" warns of a section of road near a children's facility, where children are likely to appear on the carriageway.

s2842: Below what age is it prohibited to leave a child unattended in a stopped vehicle?

s2881: Which road users must the driver of the red car give way to when moving in the direction of the arrow, if the emergency service vehicle has its flashing blue special light and siren switched on?
s2882: According to subparagraph "a" of paragraph 2 of Article 25 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, the following requirements must be met at a pedestrian crossing, in compliance with paragraph 6 of Article 21, paragraph 2 of Article 33 and paragraph 11 of Article 34 of this Law: a) if traffic is controlled by traffic lights or a traffic officer, when the signal prohibits movement the driver must stop before the pedestrian crossing or at the transverse marking in front of it, and when allowed to continue must not obstruct or endanger pedestrians who have stepped onto the crossing. If the driver is turning into another road at whose entrance there is a pedestrian crossing, the turn must be made only at low speed, and if necessary the driver must stop and let pedestrians who are on or stepping onto the crossing go across. According to paragraph 2 of Article 51 of the same Law, when an emergency or special service vehicle approaches with its flashing blue special light and siren switched on and/or giving signals through a loudspeaker, road users must make way on the carriageway for it, and for any vehicle it is escorting with dipped headlights on, and stop if necessary.
